text:
netbot: INCIDENT ALERT: stream-api p95/p99 latency breach detected across eu-west-1 -> us-east-1 cross-zone requests. Paging oncall: @irene :rotating_light:

irene: I’m on it. seeing p95 ~ 1.2s (normally 120-180ms), p99 ~ 3.6s. Streaming stalls reported (heartbeat gaps). Which clusters showing most packet loss?

sasha: network metrics: increased inter-AZ latency starting 2026-03-11T09:03Z, packet loss spikes ~2-4% on NAT gateways in eu-west-1b, and DNS timeouts rose 0.8%. TLS handshake latency jitter also up.

tj: confirmed from tracing — many requests are routing to us-east-1 replicas due to health-check flapping in eu-west-1c. KV cache misses on replicas cause tail latency.

mohan: is this the same NAT scaling issue we had last quarter? Looks like per-path queueing on nat-gw-03.

irene: put mitigation plan: 1) divert cross-zone traffic to same-zone model replicas where possible 2) increase nat gateways capacity in eu-west-1 3) temporarily disable aggressive health-check thresholds to stop flapping 4) turn on streaming degraded-mode (drop non-essential debug frames).

alice: +1 to diverting. How do we route to same-zone replicas? netbot, any existing route policy?

netbot: we have a routing-policy called prefer-same-az for model-routing. It’s been off for some customers due to canary tests. I can enable it for global tier-1 routes. Requires a quick config push:

```
# enable prefer-same-az on service route table
redwoodctl routes update --service stream-api --policy prefer-same-az --env prod
```

deploy-bot: deploy started: routes update (id: r-20260311-01). Expected rollout 30s. :rocket:

irene: doing health-check tweak now: increasing consecutive-fail threshold from 2 -> 6 for model replicas in eu-west-1. This prevents immediate failover while we stabilize.

ben: customer-ops: CS notified impacted customers in EU + US about degraded streaming; posting mitigation ETA 20-30m.

mohan: scaling nat gateways: issuing API call to add an additional NAT in eu-west-1b. Command: `cloudctl nat create --region eu-west-1 --az eu-west-1b --type t3-high-conn`

sasha: DNS team: seeing spike in UDP retries to our internal resolver; switching to tcp fallback increased handshake time. We pushed resolver health check into passive mode so clients won't failover aggressively.

irene: update: route policy rolled out. Initial telemetry: 35% of requests now staying in same AZ, p95 dropped to ~360ms for those. Overall p95 now 780ms. Still elevated but trending down.

mohan: new NAT up, BGP session established. Observed fewer retransmits on paths via nat-gw-04. Packet loss in eu-west-1b down to 0.3%.

tj: tracing after route change: end-to-end comsat shows reduced KV cache misses for same-az requests. Streaming stalls are less frequent but there are still TLS handshake outliers. Maybe subordinate CA OCSP checks are timing out?

alice: can we short-circuit OCSP or use cached validations for now? Security okay with temporary caching?

irene: security-approved for a 1h cached validation for internal service-to-service TLS, applying ACL to avoid external exposure. Patch will be applied to proxy fleet.

netbot: patch queued to proxies: enable ocsp-cache ttl=3600 for internal_domain redwood.local. Rolling restart of proxy pool in eu-west-1c started.

deploy-bot: proxy restart started: rolling 1/20 nodes (id: proxy-roll-20260311-1). Estimated 12 minutes.

customer-success: updated customers: "We’re seeing reduced errors and improving latency; streaming may still experience short stalls while we complete mitigations. Next update in 15 minutes"

irene: quick check: p99 currently 1.8s, p95 520ms. Good progress. Need to keep an eye on cross-zone traffic for next 30m.

ben: relay from major customer: "We see intermittent stalls in streaming playground; sessions sometimes reconnect." They asked for ETA. I replied 30-45m.

mohan: network logs show a small percentage of traffic still being NATed through us-east-1 — some routes didn't pick up prefer-same-az due to old route cache TTL at edge proxies. Forcing cache invalidation now.

sasha: invalidation pushed to edge-proxies: `edgectl cache invalidate routes stream-api --region eu-west-1`. Confirming purge across 50 edges.

irene: after purge, same-az ratio now 92% for eu-west-1 traffic. Observed p95 210ms for same-az requests, overall p95 300ms, p99 650ms. Streaming stalls reduced to <0.1% of sessions.

tj: reopening postmortem checklist: collect tcpdump samples on nat-gw-03 pre-mitigation (already archived), health-check logs, route table diffs, proxy OCSP latencies, and model replica failover traces.

alice: note for postmortem: consider adjusting route cache TTLs and adding proactive NAT autoscale alarms based on retransmit rate and queue size.

netbot: closing the immediate alert in ~10m if metrics hold. Will keep page open for on-call handoff.

irene: handing off to tj for follow-up during night shift. Summary for handoff: root cause — transient NAT gateway queueing + DNS resolver UDP retry causing TLS handshake jitter; secondary cause — aggressive health-check thresholds causing cross-zone failover and KV cache misses. Mitigations — prefer-same-az routing, additional NAT gateway, OCSP cache, relax health-checks. Customer impact — streaming stalls and elevated tail latency across EU + some cross-zone US traffic, ~15-40% increased error/retry surface for 25 minutes.

 tj: I’m taking post-incident action items. Will verify autoscale rules, add alert for nat-gw retransmit >1% and route flapping >3/min. Also will schedule a network runbook update for cross-zone failover steps.

customer-success: sending final customer update: "Systems stable, reduced latency and streaming interruptions. Engineering performing follow-up and posting an incident summary. Reach out for specific session logs."

netbot: ALERT STATUS: resolved (for now). Will re-open if metrics exceed thresholds.

irene: thanks team. Please add any logs/links to the incident doc. I’ll start the postmortem draft.

sasha: adding diagnostics: link to pcap archive: s3://redwood-incidents/1766501240/pcap.tar.gz, route-diff: s3://redwood-incidents/1766501240/route-diff.json, traceroutes: s3://redwood-incidents/1766501240/traces/.

ben: recorded timeline for customer success. Handing to tj for action items.

 tj: ack — will follow up in #eng-network with full RCA and an action item board. Closing thread in 30m unless new alerts appear.

alice: nice work, team. Moral: prefer-same-az should be on by default for streaming-critical routes unless a canary is explicitly running.

netbot: thread auto-note: incident duration 23m 33s.

irene: marking for postmortem and assigning owners: tj (lead), sasha (network), mohan (infra), alice (routing), ben (customer comms).

deploy-bot: logs: route update applied at 2026-03-11T09:11:12Z, nat-gw add completed 09:18:03Z, proxy ocsp cache applied 09:23:40Z.

customer-success: thanks all, closing customer-visible incident.

netbot: thread closed at 1766502473.
